title_en: Gao Guang v. Sanya Tiantong International Hotel Co., Ltd., Hainan Bochao Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Sanya South Coast Tourism Service Co., Ltd., Beijing Tianshi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — third-party revocation action
ruling_gist_en: Shareholders and the company are inherently a community of interests. The external transactions of a company and the outcomes of its civil litigation generally affect the company's asset situation, thereby indirectly affecting shareholders' returns. Since the interests of the company and the shareholders are aligned, the company's external activities should be presumed to reflect the overall will of the shareholders, and the company's claims in litigation should also be deemed to represent the overall interests of the shareholders. Therefore, although the outcome of the company's litigation may indirectly affect shareholders' interests, the shareholders' interests and opinions have already been represented by the company during the litigation process, and shareholders should not be added as third parties to participate in the company's external litigation. With respect to a binding judgment or ruling in a company's external litigation, a shareholder does not have standing to initiate a third-party revocation action.
keywords_en: civil; third-party revocation action; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Hainan Province; Beijing Municipality; natural person; legal person; Company Law; standing of shareholders to initiate third-party revocation actions; alignment of interests between shareholders and the company; company litigation representing overall interests of shareholders; dismissal of claims; shareholders' rights and interests; company's external litigation; fraudulent litigation; clarification that shareholders do not have standing to initiate third-party revocation actions
full_text_en:
Gao Guang v. Sanya Tiantong International Hotel Co., Ltd., Hainan Bochao Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., et al. — action to set aside a judgment by a third party

**Ruling Summary**

A shareholder and the company form a natural community of interests. The company's external transactions and the outcome of civil litigation generally affect the company's assets and thus indirectly affect the shareholders' returns. Because the interests of the company and its shareholders are aligned, the company's external activities should be presumed to reflect the collective will of the shareholders, and the company's assertions in litigation should also be deemed to represent the overall interests of the shareholders. Therefore, although the result of a company's litigation may indirectly affect the shareholders' interests, since the shareholders' interests and opinions have already been represented by the company in the litigation process, shareholders should not be added as third parties to participate in the company's external lawsuits. With respect to effective judgments in lawsuits against third parties involving the company, shareholders do not have standing to initiate an action to set aside the judgment as a third party.

**Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court**
(2017) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 63

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Gao Guang, male, Han Chinese, born on October 23, 1957, residing in Nangang District, Harbin City, Heilongjiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Gao Wenxiang, lawyer at Hainan Zhengyi Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Sanya Tiantong International Hotel Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 199 Sanya Bay Road, Sanya City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Dong Shijun, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongwei, lawyer at Beijing Haotian Xinhe Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Hainan Bochao Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room B3-102, Huayu Tingyuan, No. 3 Shengjing West Road, Haidian Island, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Zou Chunjin, General Manager of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Sanya South Coast Tourism Service Co., Ltd. Domicile: Area 2-2, Haipo Holiday Development Zone, Sanya City, Hainan Province (Haipo Taoran Holiday Resort).

Legal Representative: Wang Shengguo, General Manager of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Tianshi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 536 Huaisha Road, Bohai Town, Huairou District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Baoyu, Executive Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongwei, lawyer at Beijing Haotian Xinhe Law Firm.

Appellant Gao Guang, in the case of the action to set aside a judgment by a third party against appellees Sanya Tiantong International Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tiantong Company), Hainan Bochao Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bochao Company), Sanya South Coast Tourism Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as South Coast Company), and Beijing Tianshi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianshi Company), appealed against the civil ruling (2015) Qiong Civil First Instance No. 43 (hereinafter referred to as the first-instance ruling) rendered by the Hainan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Hainan High Court) to this Court. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the trial, which has now concluded.

Gao Guang's appeal requests: Request to set aside the first-instance ruling of the Hainan High Court and that this case should be tried by the Hainan High Court. Facts and reasons: (1) Gao Guang has standing to bring this action to set aside the judgment as a third party and has the right to request the revocation of the civil judgment (2012) Qiong Civil First Instance No. 3 (hereinafter referred to as Civil Judgment No. 3). First, Gao Guang is a third party without independent claims who should have participated in the case of Civil Judgment No. 3. The final outcome of Civil Judgment No. 3 involves the obligations of Bochao Company, and as a shareholder holding 50% of the equity in Bochao Company, Gao Guang's rights and interests are naturally affected by Bochao Company's assumption of obligations. On one hand, the first-instance ruling recognizes that Gao Guang has rights and interests in Bochao Company based on his equity, but on the other hand, it finds that Gao Guang has no legal interest in the outcome of Civil Judgment No. 3, which is self-contradictory. Second, although Bochao Company is an independent legal person and independently bears civil liability, Article 4 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law) expressly provides that shareholders of a company enjoy the rights to asset returns, participation in major decisions, and selection of managers in accordance with the law. The Civil Judgment No. 3 case rendered its judgment based on the "Agreement," which was signed by Zou Chunjin without the consent of the shareholders' meeting. Zou Chunjin transferred all of Bochao Company's property in the name of Bochao Company, which constitutes a "major decision," and his actions directly damaged Gao Guang's right as a shareholder to participate in major decisions and directly damaged the shareholder's right to asset returns from the company. Therefore, Gao Guang clearly has a legal interest in the case of Civil Judgment No. 3. Third, from another perspective, Gao Guang is also a third party with independent claims who should have participated in the case of Civil Judgment No. 3. The first-instance ruling found that the payment vouchers submitted by Gao Guang could not prove that he paid RMB 16,945,000 for the auction of the land of Bihai Huayun Resort, which was an erroneous finding. Gao Guang has consistently claimed in the case for dissolution of the company that he paid RMB 16,945,000 for the auction of the land, and the other shareholder of the company, Zou Chunjin, and Bochao Company have never raised any objection, indicating that the land was indeed acquired by Gao Guang through auction, thus he has independent claims. (2) Civil Judgment No. 3 found the facts incorrectly. The parties in that case maliciously colluded to forge the "Agreement" and other evidence, which in fact constituted a sham lawsuit. Gao Guang's rights were harmed by Civil Judgment No. 3, and he has the right to exercise the right of revocation. (3) This case has new evidence proving that Gao Guang has the right of action. The Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province (hereinafter referred to as Haikou Intermediate Court) issued a civil ruling (2014) Haizhong Fa Qing (Suan) Zi No. 2 on March 18, 2016, ruling to terminate the liquidation proceedings of Bochao Company. This indicates that Bochao Company was deregistered without liquidation, and shareholders or contributors should be made parties in accordance with the law. Therefore, Gao Guang, as a shareholder, may become a party in this case in accordance with the law. In summary, the first-instance ruling found facts unclearly and applied the law erroneously. Request that the court of second instance support Gao Guang's appeal requests.

Tiantong Company, Bochao Company, South Coast Company, and Tianshi Company did not submit defense opinions.

Gao Guang filed a first-instance lawsuit with the Hainan High Court, requesting: to set aside all contents of Civil Judgment No. 3, and to order the return and registration of the land use rights of 15,370.84 square meters and the above-ground buildings of 29,851.05 square meters located in the Haipo Holiday Resort Area, Sanya Bay Road, Sanya City, under the name of Bochao Company.

The Hainan High Court found the following facts upon first-instance trial:

On November 3, 2005, Gao Guang and Zou Chunjin, as shareholders (promoters), jointly established Bochao Company, with the enterprise type being a limited liability company and a registered capital of RMB 10,000,000. Gao Guang and Zou Chunjin each contributed RMB 5,000,000, with each holding 50% of the capital contribution. Zou Chunjin served as the executive director and legal representative of the company. During the period from May 31, 2006, to December 29, 2009, Tianshi Company transferred funds to Bochao Company 15 times, totaling RMB 388,000,000, with the purpose recorded on the payment vouchers as "investment funds."

On March 31, 2012, the Meilan District People's Court of Haikou City, Hainan Province, rendered administrative judgments (2012) Mei Xing Chu Zi No. 1 and No. 2, holding that the "Amendment to the Articles of Association of Bochao Company" constituted false materials and ordered the revocation of the specific administrative acts of the Hainan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce in making industrial and commercial registration changes for Bochao Company on October 22, 2009, and May 31, 2010, respectively, and reissuing the "Business License for Enterprise Legal Person" to Bochao Company. On July 10, 2012, the Haikou Intermediate Court rendered administrative judgments (2012) Haizhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 63 and No. 64, dismissing the appeals and affirming the original judgments.

On August 1, 2012, Tiantong Company filed a lawsuit with the Hainan High Court against Bochao Company and South Coast Company as defendants, and Tianshi Company as a third party, requesting: 1. Confirmation that the ownership of the Bihai Huayun Hotel (now Tiantong International Hotel) (including the land use rights within the scope of the building) belongs to Tiantong Company; 2. That Bochao Company and South Coast Company should handle the ownership transfer procedures for the building and land use rights of Tiantong International Hotel for Tiantong Company; 3. That Bochao Company should deliver all engineering materials and settlement materials for the hotel project construction to Tiantong Company; 4. That Bochao Company should pay liquidated damages of RMB 7,200,000 to Tiantong Company (provisionally calculated as of the date of filing); 5. That all litigation costs of this case be borne by Bochao Company and South Coast Company. The Hainan High Court filed the case on August 9, 2012, with case number (2012) Qiong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3. During the trial of that case, the following facts were found: On June 16, 2011, Bochao Company as Party A, South Coast Company as Party B, Tiantong Company as Party C, and Tianshi Company as Party D, jointly signed the "Agreement," which took effect on the date of signing. The "Agreement" made clear provisions on the current status, investment amount, hotel property confirmation, procedures for hotel property transfer, project settlement and transfer of settlement materials, and liability for breach of contract concerning the Bihai Huayun Hotel (now Tiantong International Hotel) located in the Haipo Development Zone, Sanya Bay, Sanya City, Hainan Province. On October 25, 2012, the Hainan High Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 3: "1. Confirm that the ownership of the building and land use rights of Bihai Huayun Hotel (i.e., Tiantong International Hotel) belongs to Tiantong Company; 2. Bochao Company and South Coast Company shall, within thirty days after this judgment takes effect, transfer the ownership of the building and land use rights of Bihai Huayun Hotel (i.e., Tiantong International Hotel) to Tiantong Company; 3. Bochao Company shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, deliver all engineering materials and settlement materials for the Bihai Huayun Hotel (i.e., Tiantong International Hotel) project construction to Tiantong Company; 4. Bochao Company shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 7,200,000 to Tiantong Company within ten days after this judgment takes effect." After the judgment was rendered, none of the parties appealed.

On August 28, 2012, Gao Guang filed a lawsuit requesting dissolution of the company on the grounds that the management and operation of Bochao Company had encountered serious difficulties, and that continued existence would cause significant losses to shareholders' interests. On September 12, 2013, the Haikou Intermediate Court rendered a civil judgment (2013) Haizhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 5, ordering the dissolution of Bochao Company. The facts found in that judgment stated: "After Bochao Company was lawfully established, it constructed the Sanya Tiantong International Hotel project, which is currently in normal operation." Bochao Company appealed against that judgment. During the second-instance trial, Gao Guang stated: Bochao Company "was actually funded by Gao Guang, with Zou Chunjin responsible for management"; Bochao Company stated: "Bochao Company is mainly invested by Zou Chunjin, and daily operations are entrusted to a management company," "Bochao Company is currently operating normally," "there are many vouchers proving that from 2006 to 2009, funds flowed in and out between Bochao Company and other units as well as Gao Guang's personal bank card." Gao Guang stated: "These funds were repayments. Because Gao Guang injected a lot of funds into Bochao Company through other units, the transfers out by Bochao Company were for repayment," "Agricultural Machinery Company is Gao Guang's own company, and Gao Guang transferred a lot of money to Bochao Company through Agricultural Machinery Company." Regarding the operation of the Tiantong International Hotel project, Bochao Company stated: "Apart from operating the Tiantong International Hotel, the company has no other business projects." Gao Guang stated: "Because the land was still under the name of South Coast Company at that time. Initially it was a cooperation, later Bochao Company bought it." On December 19, 2013, the Hainan High Court rendered a civil judgment (2013) Qiong Min Er Zhong Zi No. 35 for that case, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

On September 18, 2014, the Haikou Intermediate Court designated Hainan Tianhao Law Firm as the administrator of Bochao Company to handle the liquidation of Bochao Company. On April 20, 2015, the administrator of Bochao Company filed a lawsuit with the Hainan High Court against Tiantong Company, Tianshi Company, and South Coast Company as defendants, requesting: confirmation that the "Agreement" signed by Bochao Company on June 16, 2011, is invalid, and that the land use rights of 15,370.84 square meters and the above-ground buildings of 29,851.55 square meters located in the Haipo Holiday Resort Area, Sanya Bay Road, Sanya City, be returned and registered under the name of the administrator of Bochao Company (subject matter approximately RMB 400,000,000). After trial, the Hainan High Court held that Bochao Company had not yet been deregistered, and the administrator of Bochao Company was not a proper litigation subject, and therefore rendered a civil ruling (2015) Qiong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 23 on June 29, 2015, dismissing the lawsuit filed by the administrator of Bochao Company. After receiving the litigation documents of that case in May 2015, Tianshi Company and Tiantong Company contacted the administrator of Bochao Company and provided copies of Civil Judgment No. 3. Gao Guang then filed this action to set aside the judgment as a third party with the Hainan High Court.

Because the administrator of Bochao Company applied to terminate the liquidation proceedings on the grounds that it could not obtain the company's financial seals, accounts, and other materials and could not carry out subsequent liquidation work, the Haikou Intermediate Court issued a ruling on March 18, 2016, terminating the liquidation proceedings of Bochao Company.

Additionally, the first instance found that South Coast Company was established on April 22, 1997, with Wang Shengguo as its legal representative and investors Tian Yu and Pang Cun, whose subscribed capital contributions were 98% and 2% respectively. Tiantong Company was established on July 16, 2009, as a project company designated by Tianshi Company to operate the Bihai Huayun Hotel (now Tiantong International Hotel) after its completion, with Dong Shijun as its legal representative and investors Tian Yu and Pang Cun, whose subscribed capital contributions were 99.967% and 0.033% respectively.

South Coast Company obtained the state-owned land use right certificate Yanglan Guoyong (1997) Zi No. 0011 covering an area of 7,858.77 square meters on May 16, 1997. Bochao Company obtained the ownership of land covering an area of 7,511.07 square meters and above-ground buildings located to the south of South Coast Company's land on July 5, 2006.

Furthermore, according to the bail pending trial enforcement notice Heixinglin Jian Fan Bao Shen [2015] No. 2 issued by the People's Procuratorate of Xinglong Forestry District, Heilongjiang Province, it is recorded that the suspect Gao Guang was released on bail pending trial for suspected unit bribery, with the period starting from April 11, 2015. The notice stated that Gao Guang's work unit was Harbin Jiahe Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

During the period from 2006 to 2008, Agricultural Machinery Company, on behalf of Heilongjiang Beihong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., where Gao Guang worked, transferred funds to Bochao Company four times, totaling RMB 32,000,000. The transfer vouchers recorded: on September 17, 2007, a transfer of RMB 4,000,000, bank summary: goods payment; on November 1, 2007, a transfer of RMB 5,000,000, bank summary: goods payment; on February 26, 2008, a transfer of RMB 3,000,000, bank summary: goods payment; on April 3, 2008, a transfer of RMB 20,000,000, bank summary: repayment. Bochao Company had transferred funds to Agricultural Machinery Company five times and made one payment on its behalf, totaling RMB 60,300,000, with the bank summary as "current account."

The Hainan High Court held that this case is an action to set aside a judgment by a third party. Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), a third party in the original trial who was unable to participate in the proceedings due to reasons not attributable to himself or herself has the right to file an action to set aside the judgment. Based on the arguments of both parties, the issue in dispute in this case is: Whether Gao Guang is a third party in the case of Civil Judgment No. 3, and whether his action to set aside the judgment as a third party complies with legal provisions.

Regarding the issue of whether Gao Guang is a third party in the case of Civil Judgment No. 3, Gao Guang stated in his written complaint that he applied to set aside the original judgment as a third party with independent claims based on his shareholder status, but changed his statement during the first-instance trial, claiming he was a third party without independent claims.

(I) Regarding whether Gao Guang is a third party with independent claims. A third party with independent claims must have substantive rights and interests in the subject matter of the original trial. First, the legal relationship adjudicated in the case of Civil Judgment No. 3 was a contractual relationship for joint venture and cooperative development of real estate, and Gao Guang was not a party to that contract. Second, Gao Guang claimed that Bochao Company was his personal company and that he paid all investments and daily expenses of the company. However, Gao Guang only provided evidence showing that he made several transfers to Bochao Company through Agricultural Machinery Company. After cross-checking with Bochao Company's bank account records, there were fund flows between Bochao Company and Agricultural Machinery Company, with the bank account recording the purpose as "current account" and "goods payment," etc. It cannot be determined that all investments in Bochao Company were made by Gao Guang. Gao Guang claimed that he personally paid RMB 16,945,000 for the auction of the land, but the payment vouchers he submitted failed to prove that the payment was for the auction of the land of Bihai Huayun Resort. The industrial and commercial registration of Bochao Company shows that shareholders Zou Chunjin and Gao Guang each hold 50% equity. Gao Guang failed to prove that Bochao Company was owned solely by Gao Guang, so the property rights and interests of Bochao Company cannot be equated with Gao Guang's personal property rights and interests. Third, the disputed land and above-ground buildings do not belong to Gao Guang. Among the land use rights of the land where the Tiantong International Hotel in dispute is located, the land use rights of 7,858.77 square meters have been registered under South Coast Company since May 1997, and the land use rights of 7,511.07 square meters have been registered under Bochao Company since July 2006. Gao Guang is neither a party to that contract nor does he have any rights to the disputed land and above-ground buildings. Therefore, Gao Guang is not a third party with independent claims.

(2) Whether Gao Guang is a third party without independent claims. A third party without independent claims must have a legal interest in the outcome of the case. First, Gao Guang claims that Civil Judgment No. 3 infringes upon the property rights and interests of Bochao Company, involving Gao Guang's right to earnings on assets and right to participate in decision-making as a shareholder of Bochao Company, and thus he has a legal interest in the outcome of Civil Judgment No. 3. The Hainan High People's Court held that Article 36, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A legal person is an organization that has the capacity for civil rights and capacity for civil conduct, and independently enjoys civil rights and assumes civil obligations in accordance with the law." Article 3 of the Company Law provides: "A company is an enterprise legal person, has independent legal person property, and enjoys the right to legal person property. A company shall be liable for its debts with all its property. Shareholders of a limited liability company shall be liable to the company to the extent of their subscribed capital contributions; shareholders of a joint stock limited company shall be liable to the company to the extent of the shares they subscribe for." In this case, Bochao Company is a limited liability company with independent legal person status. Gao Guang is a shareholder of Bochao Company and has no right to dispose of the company's property; he can only enjoy rights in the company based on his shares. Civil Judgment No. 3 confirmed that the ownership of the houses and the right to use the land of Bihai Huayun Hotel (i.e., Tiantong International Hotel) belong to Tiantong Company, and ordered Bochao Company and Nanhai'an Company to complete the transfer and registration within a time limit, deliver relevant engineering and settlement materials, and pay liquidated damages, among other matters. That judgment only confirmed the responsibilities and obligations of Bochao Company and did not impose civil liability or obligations on Gao Guang. Therefore, Gao Guang has no legal interest in the outcome of the original trial of Case No. 3. If Gao Guang believes that Zou Chunjin, another shareholder of Bochao Company, has infringed upon his shareholder's property rights, he may file a separate claim. Second, Gao Guang claims that Tiantong International Hotel was built solely by Bochao Company, that there was no cooperative development relationship, that the four-party "Agreement" is a false contract, and that Zou Chunjin and Tianshi Company maliciously colluded to transfer Bochao Company's property, infringing upon his right to earnings on assets and right to participate in major decision-making as a shareholder. Upon investigation, during the period of investment and construction of the hotel project, Tianshi Company made a total of 15 transfers to Bochao Company amounting to RMB 388 million, with the bank records indicating the purpose as "investment funds." The construction unit for the planning, construction approval, and completion acceptance registration of Tiantong International Hotel was Bochao Company and Nanhai'an Company. In fact, Tiantong Company and Nanhai'an Company are the same investors. Gao Guang also stated that Bochao Company indeed cooperated with Nanhai'an Company in the development and construction of Bihai Huayun Hotel (i.e., Tiantong International Hotel). Although he claimed that Nanhai'an Company had withdrawn from the cooperation, he did not submit any evidence to prove this. Gao Guang failed to provide evidence proving that the parties in Civil Judgment No. 3 maliciously colluded to transfer Bochao Company's property and caused Civil Judgment No. 3 to be erroneous, potentially harming Gao Guang's personal civil rights and interests. Civil Judgment No. 3 did not impose any payment obligation on Gao Guang personally. Gao Guang has no legal interest in the outcome of the original trial and is not a third party without independent claims.

In summary, Gao Guang is not a third party in Civil Judgment No. 3 and does not have the standing to bring a third-party revocation action under Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law; therefore, his lawsuit should be dismissed in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 56, Article 119, and Item 3 of Paragraph 1 of Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law, and Article 208 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Hainan High People's Court ruled as follows:

Gao Guang's lawsuit is dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 2,041,800 prepaid by Gao Guang shall be refunded.

The facts found by this Court upon review in the second instance are the same as those found in the first-instance ruling.

Upon trial, this Court holds that this case is a third-party revocation action filed by Gao Guang against the effective Civil Judgment No. 3 of the Hainan High People's Court. According to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law, a third party who fails to participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to himself may file an action to revoke a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation statement. The first-instance ruling of the Hainan High People's Court held that Gao Guang does not have the standing as a third party under Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law and dismissed his lawsuit. Gao Guang appealed this ruling, so the second instance shall focus on whether Gao Guang has the standing to bring a third-party revocation action.

The function of the third-party revocation action system is primarily to protect the legitimate rights and interests of a third party who did not participate in the original lawsuit and was harmed by an erroneous effective judgment. When a third party fails to participate in the original lawsuit for reasons beyond its own control, resulting in an erroneous judgment by the people's court, the law grants that third party, who should have participated in the original lawsuit, the right to revoke the original effective judgment by filing a separate lawsuit. Therefore, a person bringing a third-party revocation action must meet the status requirements of a third party who should have participated in the original lawsuit. Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 2 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law provide for two types of third parties entitled to bring a revocation action: the third party with independent claims and the third party without independent claims. The first-instance ruling has found that Civil Judgment No. 3 case was a dispute over a joint venture and cooperative development of real estate contract, with Tiantong Company as the plaintiff, Bochao Company and Nanhai'an Company as defendants, and Tianshi Company as a third party. This Court holds that Gao Guang does not meet the conditions for participating in that case as a third party. The reasons are as follows:

First, Gao Guang has no independent claim regarding the subject matter of the lawsuit in Civil Judgment No. 3 and is not a third party with independent claims in that case. A third party with independent claims refers to a person who has the right to file a claim as an independent entity with substantive rights against the subject matter in dispute between the parties. In Civil Judgment No. 3, Tiantong Company filed various claims based on the four-party "Agreement" between it, Bochao Company, Nanhai'an Company, and Tianshi Company, including a request to confirm that the ownership of the houses (including the right to use the land within the house area) of Bihai Huayun Hotel belongs to Tiantong Company and a request for Bochao Company to pay liquidated damages. The Hainan High People's Court tried and rendered judgment based on the provisions of the "Agreement." Gao Guang is only a shareholder of Bochao Company and is not a party to the "Agreement," so he cannot file claims based on that agreement. Furthermore, regarding the land registered under Bochao Company's name that was the subject of the transaction under the "Agreement," Gao Guang claims that he personally paid RMB 16.945 million to bid for the land. Even if Gao Guang's claim is valid, since the land has been registered under Bochao Company's name, it indicates that the land has been converted into legal person property. According to the relevant provisions of the Company Law, the property of a legal person and the property of its shareholders are independent. Although Gao Guang, as a shareholder of the company, has the right to earnings on assets, he cannot directly claim substantive rights over the legal person's property. Therefore, Gao Guang cannot participate in Civil Judgment No. 3 as a third party with independent claims.

Second, Gao Guang does not qualify as a third party without independent claims in Civil Judgment No. 3. A third party without independent claims refers to a person who, although having no independent claim regarding the subject matter of the lawsuit between the parties, has a legal interest in the outcome of the case. The legal interest that a third party has in the outcome of the case may be direct or indirect. In this case, Civil Judgment No. 3 only confirmed the legal obligations to be borne by Bochao Company and did not impose civil liability on Gao Guang. Therefore, Gao Guang does not have a direct interest in the outcome of Civil Judgment No. 3. Regarding the issue of whether there is an indirect interest, generally speaking, shareholders and the company are a natural community of interests. Shareholders of a company have the right to earnings on the company's assets. The company's external transactions and the outcome of civil litigation generally affect the company's assets, thereby indirectly affecting shareholders' earnings rights. From this perspective, shareholders have an indirect legal interest in the outcome of civil litigation involving the company. However, because the interests of the company and its shareholders are aligned, the company's external activities should be presumed to reflect the overall will of its shareholders, and the positions taken by the company in litigation should also be deemed to represent the overall interests of the shareholders. Therefore, even though the outcome of a company's lawsuit may indirectly affect the interests of its shareholders, the shareholders' interests and opinions have already been represented and expressed by the company during the litigation process, and shareholders should not be added as third parties to participate in the litigation. In this case, although Gao Guang is a shareholder of Bochao Company, during the litigation activities of Bochao Company with Nanhai'an Company, Tianshi Company, and Tiantong Company, the opinions of the shareholders were already represented by Bochao Company. Therefore, Gao Guang, as a shareholder, should not participate in that case as a third party without independent claims.

As for conflicts of interest arising from differences among shareholders, these fall within the internal legal relationship of the company and should be dealt with in accordance with the law between shareholders, or between shareholders and the company. Article 20 of the Company Law provides that shareholders of a company shall abide by laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association, exercise shareholder rights in accordance with the law, and shall not abuse their shareholder rights to harm the interests of the company or other shareholders; nor shall they abuse the independent legal person status of the company and the limited liability of shareholders to harm the interests of the company's creditors. If a shareholder abuses his shareholder rights and causes losses to the company or other shareholders, he shall bear compensation liability in accordance with the law. In this case, Gao Guang claims that Zou Chunjin, using the name of Bochao Company, transferred all of Bochao Company's property and entered into the "Agreement" without the approval of the shareholders' meeting, thereby harming the rights and interests of shareholder Gao Guang. According to the above analysis, the facts alleged by Gao Guang involve internal legal relationships among shareholders and may be dealt with separately in accordance with the law.

In summary, Gao Guang does not meet the status requirements for participating in Civil Judgment No. 3 as a third party and does not have the standing to bring an action to revoke Civil Judgment No. 3. The Hainan High People's Court's ruling dismissing Gao Guang's lawsuit on this basis is correct, and this Court hereby affirms it in accordance with the law. As for Gao Guang's appeal claims that Civil Judgment No. 3 contains errors in fact finding, constitutes a fraudulent lawsuit, and that Tiantong Company, Bochao Company, Nanhai'an Company, and Tianshi Company engaged in malicious collusion, these are matters within the substantive trial of a third-party revocation action. Since Gao Guang does not have the standing for a third-party revocation action and does not meet the conditions for filing a lawsuit, this Court need not further examine the aforementioned substantive issues in this case.

Pursuant to Item 1 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 and Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original ruling is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
